answer.effective_date: Effective Date: April 1, 2026; Last Revised (Annual Review approved): March 23, 2026
criteria_quotes: Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met: There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following: Degenerative joint disease (DJD), Osteoarthritis (OA), Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), Traumatic arthritis, or Avascular necrosis AND Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following: Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration OR Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration AND Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following: Irregular joint surfaces, Glenoid sclerosis, Glenoid osteophyte changes, Flattened glenoid, Cystic changes in the humeral head, or Joint space narrowing AND Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics, or Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate AND A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: Physical therapy, Activity modification, or Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises

OR Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions: Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union; Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue; Failed hemi-arthroplasty; Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction

Total shoulder, reverse total shoulder, or hemi-arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when the above medical necessity criteria are not met. Total shoulder, reverse total shoulder, or hemi-arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when ANY of the following are present: Active infection of the joint or active systemic bacteremia; Active skin infection or open wound within the planned surgical site; Allergy to components of the implant; Deltoid deficiency; Inadequate bone stock to support implantation of prosthesis; Neuropathic (Charcot) arthropathy of the shoulder; Paralytic disorder of the shoulder; Rapidly progressive neurological disease

Documentation Requirements: For a total shoulder arthroplasty and degenerative joint disease such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis or traumatic arthritis or osteonecrosis ALL of the following are present: Needs treatment because of disabling pain and/or limited shoulder function interfering with activities of daily living (ADLs) AND Imaging evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery ... AND History of unsuccessful three-month trial of failed non-operative conservative management ... and a 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: physical therapy, or flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, or reasonable restriction of activities.
answer.appeal_deadline: As stated in the denial letter, the appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (2026-08-07), i.e., by 2027-02-03.
answer.submission_route: Mail the completed 'Member Appeal' form and supporting documentation to: Premera Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alaska, Member Appeals, P.O. Box 21762, Eagan, MN 55121. Fax: 866-903-9899. The form must be signed by the member (or legal guardian/authorized representative with documentation). Questions can be directed to Customer Service at the number on the back of the member ID card, or via the Secure Inbox after signing in at premera.com. (Note: a separate general Premera appeals fax of 425-918-5592 and PO Box 91102, Seattle, WA 98111-9202 also appears in some Premera materials for provider/other appeals and civil-rights grievances — the member should use the address/fax on the 'How to File an Appeal for a Member' form, P.O. Box 21762, Eagan, MN 55121, fax 866-903-9899, to be safe, or call the number on the ID card to confirm the correct routing for this specific denial.)
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The criteria quoted above were pulled directly from the publicly posted PDF of Medical Policy 7.01.590 'Shoulder Arthroplasty' on Premera's individual-plan medical policy site. To be certain this is the exact version applied to this specific pre-authorization decision, the patient/provider should also request from Premera (via Customer Service or the appeals contact) a copy of 'the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria relied upon in this determination,' which insurers are required to provide free of charge upon request during an appeal under ACA/ERISA-type claims regulations. The denial letter itself does not cite a policy number, so this should be explicitly requested and cross-checked.
answer.notes: 1) The denial letter does not name a specific policy number, so I identified the policy by matching CPT 23472 to Premera's individual-plan medical policy library; Premera's own policy index and update pages confirm 7.01.590 is the correct, currently-applicable medical necessity policy for CPT 23472 (total shoulder arthroplasty) as of the 2026-08-07 denial date. 2) There are parallel Premera policy documents for 'employer group' plans (URL path /medicalpolicies/7.01.590.pdf, referenced by the related-policy citation in 7.01.605) versus 'individual/ACA' plans (path /medicalpolicies-individual/7.01.590.pdf); since the plan here is described as Commercial/ACA, I used the individual-plan version, which is the one actually retrieved. Confirm with Premera/provider which specific version (group vs. individual) was applied, since language could differ slightly. 3) Two different appeal mailing addresses/fax numbers appear across Premera's public materials (member appeals: PO Box 21762, Eagan MN, fax 866-903-9899; vs. a general Complaints and Appeals PO Box 91102, Seattle WA, fax 425-918-5592, used for civil rights grievances and in some provider-facing pages). The patient should call the Customer Service number on the back of the ID card to confirm the correct current address for filing a member medical-necessity appeal, and should also ask Premera directly to identify the exact policy document and version number they applied to this claim, requesting it in writing as part of the appeal file.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-07
Member: Taylor Lawson
Member ID: W261288012
Plan: Premera Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alaska (Commercial/ACA), state of Alaska

Dear Taylor,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Total shoulder replacement
    Procedure code (CPT): 23472

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-03).

Reference number: POC-F781755028-57061


---

Above is a denial letter. Using web search as needed:

1. Identify the payer's governing medical policy for the denied procedure --
   the specific document containing the medical-necessity criteria this payer
   applies to this CPT code.
2. Give its title, policy number, URL, and effective or last-revised date.
3. Quote the medical-necessity criteria the patient must address.
4. State the appeal deadline.
5. State where and how to submit the appeal.

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how
the patient can obtain the criteria that were applied to them.

Answer as JSON with keys: policy_found (true/false), policy_title,
policy_number, policy_url, effective_date, criteria_quotes (list),
appeal_deadline, submission_route, how_to_obtain_criteria, confidence, notes.
